title: Act Five. Radha-sangama (Union with Radha)
html:
Dawn after the night in the grove; Madanika tells Shashimukhi of the meeting of Radha and Madhava; Radha, abashed, returns in the light of morning; an alarm behind the scenes — the bull-demon Arishtasura has burst into Vraja; Krishna slays him; Madanika again unites Radha with Krishna; the closing benediction.

(Enter Shashimukhi.)

Shashimukhi (Prakrit). Ah, I don't know what happened today in the grove with those two intent on bliss. I'll follow the lady and find out. (Looking ahead.) Ah, here she comes, slowly, slowly, her eyes closed with sleep. (Using Sanskrit.)

Verse 2

स्वैरं स्वैरं कथमपि दृशौ मन्दनिष्पन्दतारे
विन्यस्यन्ती शिथिलितभुजद्वन्द्वसंनामितांसा ।
मन्दन्यासस्खलितचरणव्यस्तमञ्जीरघोषा
देवी निद्राकुलतरतनुर्मोदमाविष्करोति ॥ २ ॥

svairaṁ svairaṁ kathamapi dṛśau mandaniṣpandatāre
vinyasyantī śithilitabhujadvandvasaṁnāmitāṁsā |
mandanyāsaskhalitacaraṇavyastamañjīraghoṣā
devī nidrākulataratanurmodamāviṣkaroti || 2 ||

svairaṁ svairam — slowly, slowly; katham api — somehow; dṛśau — the eyes; manda-niṣpanda-tāre — with almost motionless pupils; vinyasyantī — directing; śithilita-bhuja-dvandva-saṁnāmita-aṁsā — her shoulders drooping with slack arms; manda-nyāsa-skhalita-caraṇa-vyasta-mañjīra-ghoṣā — her feet faltering with slow steps and her anklets' jingle broken; devī — the lady; nidrā-ākulatara-tanuḥ — her body overcome by sleep; modam — joy; āviṣkaroti — reveals.

2Slowly, slowly, somehow lifting her eyes with their almost motionless pupils, her shoulders drooping and her arms hanging loose, stepping so languidly that her feet falter and the jingling of her anklets falters too — the lady, her body wholly overcome by sleep, shows her joy.1

Song 18 — in raga Sukha-sindhura.

Song 18 (3)

दरमुकुलारुणलोचनमाननमिह गतकान्तिविकाशं(?)
कमलमिवारुणमुषसि विधावनुबिम्बितमम्बुसकाशे ॥
किमिदमियं प्रविशन्ती भजति मनो मम
रतिविरतेव वनिता कापि चलन्ती ॥ ध्रु ॥
शिथिलभुजा मृदुरणितकनकमणिकङ्कणमिदमनुवारं
विसंकुलपादनिवेशनिवारितनूपुरललितविहारम् ॥
गजपतिरुद्रनराधिपहृदये मुदमिदमातनुतेति
रामानन्दरायकविभणितं विलसति रसिकजनेति ॥ ३ ॥

daramukulāruṇalocanamānanamiha gatakāntivikāśaṁ(?)
kamalamivāruṇamuṣasi vidhāvanubimbitamambusakāśe ||
kimidamiyaṁ praviśantī bhajati mano mama
rativirateva vanitā kāpi calantī || dhru ||
śithilabhujā mṛduraṇitakanakamaṇikaṅkaṇamidamanuvāraṁ
visaṁkulapādaniveśanivāritanūpuralalitavihāram ||
gajapatirudranarādhipahṛdaye mudamidamātanuteti
rāmānandarāyakavibhaṇitaṁ vilasati rasikajaneti || 3 ||

dara-mukula-aruṇa-locanam — with half-closed reddish eyes; ānanam — face; iha — here; gata-kānti-vikāśam — its lustre gone; kamalam iva — like a lotus; aruṇam — red; uṣasi — at dawn; vidhau — by the moon; anubimbitam — reflected; ambu-sakāśe — in the water; kim idam — what is this; iyam — she; praviśantī — entering; bhajati — appears; mano mama — to my mind; rati-viratā iva — as one after love-play; vanitā kāpi — some woman; calantī — leaving; śithila-bhujā — with slack arms; mṛdu-raṇita — softly tinkling; kanaka-maṇi-kaṅkaṇam — gold and jewelled bangle; anuvāram — again and again; visaṅkula-pāda-niveśa — by uneven placing of the feet; nivārita-nūpura-lalita-vihāram — stilling the lovely play of the anklets; gajapati-rudra-narādhipa-hṛdaye — in the heart of Gajapati Rudra; mudam — joy; ātanute — brings; rāmānanda-rāya-kavi-bhaṇitam — spoken by the poet Ramananda Raya; vilasati — sports; rasika-jane — among connoisseurs.

3Her eyes half-closed and reddish, her face here seeming to have lost its glow — like a red lotus at dawn reflected in the water beside the moon. What is this? As she enters, my mind sees in her a woman leaving after love-play. (Refrain.) Her arms are slack, and again and again her golden, jewelled bangles softly tinkle; setting her feet unevenly, she stills the jingling of her anklets, their lovely play. May these words of the poet Ramananda Raya bring joy to the heart of Gajapati Rudra, lord of men, and sport among the connoisseurs.2

(Enter Madanika, dressed as described. Rubbing her eyes, looking ahead.)

Madanika. Ah, how lovely is the close of a spring night! For:

Verse 5

इतो मन्दं मन्दं सरसिजवनीवातलहरी
ततश्चूतास्वादप्रमुदितपिकानां कलकलः ।
क्वचित्फुल्लां वल्लीमनु मधुकराणां स्वरकथा
कुतश्चित्कोकानां मृदुमधुरमानन्दलपितम् ॥ ५ ॥

ito mandaṁ mandaṁ sarasijavanīvātalaharī
tataścūtāsvādapramuditapikānāṁ kalakalaḥ |
kvacitphullāṁ vallīmanu madhukarāṇāṁ svarakathā
kutaścitkokānāṁ mṛdumadhuramānandalapitam || 5 ||

itaḥ — here; mandaṁ mandam — gently, gently; sarasija-vanī-vāta-laharī — a wave of breeze from the lotus beds; tataḥ — there; cūta-āsvāda-pramudita-pikānām — of cuckoos delighted by tasting mango; kalakalaḥ — the chatter; kvacit — somewhere; phullāṁ vallīm anu — about a blossoming creeper; madhukarāṇām — of bees; svara-kathā — the humming talk; kutaścit — from somewhere; kokānām — of the cakravakas; mṛdu-madhuram — soft and sweet; ānanda-lapitam — joyful murmur.

5Here gently, gently blows a breeze from the lotus beds; there is the chatter of cuckoos delighted by the taste of mango; somewhere, the humming of bees about a blossoming creeper; somewhere, the soft, sweet, joyful murmur of the cakravakas.3

(Walking a few steps, showing joy.)

Verse 6

उद्दामस्मरचातुरीपरिचयादन्योन्यरागादिमां
रात्रिं जागरितानि सद्मनि युवद्वन्द्वानि यच्छेरते ।
तत्तेषां श्वसितानिलेन तुलनामासादयिष्यन्निव
प्रोन्मीलत्कमलावलीषु वलते श्रीखण्डवीथीमरुत् ॥ ६ ॥

uddāmasmaracāturīparicayādanyonyarāgādimāṁ
rātriṁ jāgaritāni sadmani yuvadvandvāni yaccherate |
tatteṣāṁ śvasitānilena tulanāmāsādayiṣyanniva
pronmīlatkamalāvalīṣu valate śrīkhaṇḍavīthīmarut || 6 ||

uddāma-smara-cāturī-paricayāt — from acquaintance with the skill of ardent Smara; anyonya-rāgāt — from mutual love; imāṁ rātrim — this night; jāgaritāni — having stayed awake; sadmani — in the houses; yuva-dvandvāni — young couples; yat — since; śerate — are sleeping; tat — so; teṣām — their; śvasita-anilena — with the breath; tulanām — comparison; āsādayiṣyan iva — as if to attain; pronmīlat-kamala-āvalīṣu — over rows of opening lotuses; valate — moves; śrī-khaṇḍa-vīthī-marut — the breeze of the sandal paths.

6The young couples who, through mutual love and acquaintance with the skill of ardent Smara, stayed awake all this night, are now asleep in their houses; and as if to vie with their breathing, the wind from the sandal paths plays over the rows of opening lotuses.

(Looking ahead, in wonder.)

Verse 7

चकितचकितं क्वापि क्वापि प्रमोदनिरन्तरं
क्वचन वनिता कुण्ठोत्कुण्ठं निधाय विलोचने ।
कलयति तथावस्थामेषा रथाङ्गकुटुम्बिनी
भवति न यथा चान्तेवासी विदग्धवधूजनः ॥ ७ ॥

cakitacakitaṁ kvāpi kvāpi pramodanirantaraṁ
kvacana vanitā kuṇṭhotkuṇṭhaṁ nidhāya vilocane |
kalayati tathāvasthāmeṣā rathāṅgakuṭumbinī
bhavati na yathā cāntevāsī vidagdhavadhūjanaḥ || 7 ||

cakita-cakitam — startled, startled; kvāpi — somewhere; kvāpi — somewhere; pramoda-nirantaram — ceaselessly joyful; kvacana — somewhere; vanitā — the wife; kuṇṭha-utkuṇṭham — lowered and raised; nidhāya — setting; vilocane — her eyes; kalayati — shows; tathā-avasthām — such a state; eṣā — this; rathāṅga-kuṭumbinī — wife of the cakravaka; bhavati — becomes; na(?) — not; yathā — so that; ca — and; antevāsī — a pupil; vidagdha-vadhū-janaḥ — clever young wives.

7Here startled, startled, there unceasingly joyful, here lowering and there raising her eyes — so behaves this female cakravaka, that even clever young wives might become her pupils.4

(Going aside a moment, in amazement.) Ah, here is something lovelier still! For:

Verse 8

उन्मीलत्कमलोदरे मधुभरे दृष्ट्वानुबिम्बं निजं
मन्वाना दयितं कथंचिदधुना सोत्कण्ठया(?) धावति ।
उत्कण्ठोपनतं पुनः सहचरं दृष्ट्वा विलक्षा मुहु-
र्न स्थातुं न च गन्तुमत्र चतुरा भृङ्गी चिरं भ्राम्यति ॥ ८ ॥

unmīlatkamalodare madhubhare dṛṣṭvānubimbaṁ nijaṁ
manvānā dayitaṁ kathaṁcidadhunā sotkaṇṭhayā(?) dhāvati |
utkaṇṭhopanataṁ punaḥ sahacaraṁ dṛṣṭvā vilakṣā muhu-
rna sthātuṁ na ca gantumatra caturā bhṛṅgī ciraṁ bhrāmyati || 8 ||

unmīlat-kamala-udare — in the cup of an opening lotus; madhu-bhare — full of honey; dṛṣṭvā — seeing; anubimbam — reflection; nijam — her own; manvānā — thinking; dayitam — her beloved; kathaṁcit — somehow; adhunā — at once; sa-utkaṇṭhayā — longingly; dhāvati — darts; utkaṇṭhā-upanatam — arrived in longing; punaḥ — then; sahacaram — her companion; dṛṣṭvā — seeing; vilakṣā — abashed; muhuḥ — again and again; na sthātum — neither to stay; na ca gantum — nor to go; atra — here; caturā — the clever; bhṛṅgī — female bee; ciram — long; bhrāmyati — circles.

8Seeing her own reflection in an opening lotus full of honey and taking it for her mate, the female bee eagerly darts to it; then, seeing her true companion arriving, abashed, the clever one can neither stay nor go, and long keeps circling.5

Shashimukhi. She is so captivated by the loveliness of the morning that she does not see me. (Approaching with the words "I bow to you.") Lady, I bow to you.

Madanika. What, Shashimukhi, child! Lost in thought, I did not notice you for a long while.

Shashimukhi. Lady, why do you seem to me as if overcome by sleep?

Madanika. Child, why "as if"? I am.

Shashimukhi. But why?

Madanika.

Verse 14

राधामाधवयोरद्य निकुञ्जमधिष्ठितयोः ।
तत्कौतुकितालोकान्निशेयमतिवाहिता ॥ १४ ॥

rādhāmādhavayoradya nikuñjamadhiṣṭhitayoḥ |
tatkautukitālokānniśeyamativāhitā || 14 ||

rādhā-mādhavayoḥ — of Radha and Madhava; adya — today; nikuñjam — in the grove; adhiṣṭhitayoḥ — abiding; tat-kautukita-ālokāt — from watching their wondrous play; niśā iyam — this night; ativāhitā — has been passed.

14Today Radha and Madhava were in the grove; watching their wondrous play, I passed this night without sleep.

Shashimukhi. And what happened there?

Madanika. Listen. (Wiping her eyes.) Child, you know what happened until they entered the grove.

Shashimukhi. Of course.

Madanika. After that —

Verse 18

यस्तम्भो मुरविद्विषः समभवत्तेनापि तस्या मनो
माध्यस्थ्यं परिशङ्कते स्म(?) मनोजन्मत्रपानिर्भरम् ।
कामेषुव्रजपक्षवातविसरप्राप्तोदयो न क्षणा-
दाश्वासं हरिणीदृशो वितनुते तस्य प्रकम्पो यदि ॥ १८ ॥

yastambho muravidviṣaḥ samabhavattenāpi tasyā mano
mādhyasthyaṁ pariśaṅkate sma(?) manojanmatrapānirbharam |
kāmeṣuvrajapakṣavātavisaraprāptodayo na kṣaṇā-
dāśvāsaṁ hariṇīdṛśo vitanute tasya prakampo yadi || 18 ||

yaḥ stambhaḥ — the stupor that; mura-vidviṣaḥ — of the Enemy of Mura; samabhavat — arose; tena api — by that too; tasyāḥ — her; manaḥ — mind; mādhyasthyam — indifference; pariśaṅkate — feared; manojanma-trapā-nirbharam — full of love and shyness; kāma-iṣu-vraja-pakṣa-vāta-visara-prāpta-udayaḥ — arisen from the wind of the feathers of Kama's many arrows; na — not; kṣaṇāt — at once; āśvāsam — comfort; hariṇī-dṛśaḥ — to the doe-eyed; vitanute — would give; tasya — His; prakampaḥ — trembling; yadi — if.

18the stupor that seized the Enemy of Mura made even her mind, full of love and shyness, fear that He was indifferent; and had not His trembling, stirred by the wind of the feathers of Kama's arrows, reassured her, the doe-eyed one would not have been comforted.6

Shashimukhi. Joy, joy! I am fulfilled.

Madanika. And from here on the friends are fulfilled still more.

Shashimukhi. Did the lady see anything else?

Madanika. Everything.

Shashimukhi. And then?

Madanika. Child,

Verse 24

साशङ्कं समनोभवं प्रहसितं सापत्रपं सस्मयं
सासूयं समनोहरात्मकपदं सप्रेम सोत्कण्ठितम् ।
राधायाः मधुसूदनस्य च तदा कुञ्जे तदासीद्रतं
येनासीन्मदनोऽपि विस्मयरसस्निग्धान्तरो निर्भरम् ॥ २४ ॥

sāśaṅkaṁ samanobhavaṁ prahasitaṁ sāpatrapaṁ sasmayaṁ
sāsūyaṁ samanoharātmakapadaṁ saprema sotkaṇṭhitam |
rādhāyāḥ madhusūdanasya ca tadā kuñje tadāsīdrataṁ
yenāsīnmadano'pi vismayarasasnigdhāntaro nirbharam || 24 ||

sa-āśaṅkam — with apprehension; sa-manobhavam — with love; prahasitam — with laughter; sa-apatrapam — with shyness; sa-smayam — with pride; sa-asūyam — with jealous pique; sa-manohara-ātmaka-padam — with captivating words; sa-prema — with tenderness; sa-utkaṇṭhitam — with longing; rādhāyāḥ — of Radha; madhusūdanasya — of Madhusudana; ca — and; tadā — then; kuñje — in the grove; tat — such; āsīt — was; ratam — the love-play; yena — by which; āsīt — became; madanaḥ api — even Madana; vismaya-rasa-snigdha-antaraḥ — his heart moistened with the rasa of wonder; nirbharam — wholly.

24with apprehension and with love, with laughter, with shyness, with pride, with jealous pique, with captivating words, with tenderness, with longing — such was then in the grove the love-play of Radha and Madhusudana that Madana himself was filled with wonder.7

Song 19 — in raga Ahira.

Song 19 (25)

मृदुमञ्जीररवानुगतं गतमनया शयनसमीपं
मधुरिपुणापि पदानि कियन्त्यपि चलितं कियदनुरूपम् ॥
शशिमुखि किं तव बत कथयामि
राधामाधवकेलिभरादहमद्भुतमाकलयामि ॥ ध्रु ॥
मिलितमिदं किल तनुयुगलं पुनरपि न कञ्चन भेदं
विषमशराशुगकीलितमिव सखि गलितचिरंतनखेदम् ॥
नखररदावलिखण्डितमपि गुरु निश्वसितायतभीतं(?)
रुद्रगजाधिपमुदमातनुतां रामानन्दरायसुगीतम् ॥ २५ ॥

mṛdumañjīraravānugataṁ gatamanayā śayanasamīpaṁ
madhuripuṇāpi padāni kiyantyapi calitaṁ kiyadanurūpam ||
śaśimukhi kiṁ tava bata kathayāmi
rādhāmādhavakelibharādahamadbhutamākalayāmi || dhru ||
militamidaṁ kila tanuyugalaṁ punarapi na kañcana bhedaṁ
viṣamaśarāśugakīlitamiva sakhi galitaciraṁtanakhedam ||
nakhararadāvalikhaṇḍitamapi guru niśvasitāyatabhītaṁ(?)
rudragajādhipamudamātanutāṁ rāmānandarāyasugītam || 25 ||

mṛdu-mañjīra-rava-anugatam — accompanied by the soft jingle of anklets; gatam — went; anayā — she; śayana-samīpam — near the couch; madhu-ripuṇā api — and the Enemy of Madhu too; padāni kiyanti api — a few steps; calitam — moved; kiyad-anurūpam — correspondingly; śaśimukhi — O Shashimukhi; kim — what; tava — to you; bata — ah; kathayāmi — shall I tell; rādhā-mādhava-keli-bharāt — from the fullness of the play of Radha and Madhava; aham — I; adbhutam — a wonder; ākalayāmi — have seen; militam idam — this was united; kila — it is said; tanu-yugalam — the pair of bodies; punar api — then; na kañcana bhedam — with no difference; viṣama-śara-āśuga-kīlitam iva — as if pierced by the Odd-arrowed One's arrows; sakhi — friend; galita-cirantana-khedam — their long sorrow gone; nakhara-rada-āvali-khaṇḍitam api — though wounded by nails and teeth; guru — deeply; niśvasita — sighing; āyata-bhītam(?) — as if in fear; rudra-gajādhipa-mudam — the joy of Rudra, lord of elephants; ātanutām — may it increase; rāmānanda-rāya-sugītam — Ramananda Raya's fine song.

25To the soft jingling of her anklets she came near the couch; and the Enemy of Madhu too took a few steps towards her, in keeping with her. Shashimukhi, what shall I tell you? I have seen a wonder — the fullness of the play of Radha and Madhava! (Refrain.) And so, it is said, their two bodies were united so that no difference remained; friend, as if pierced by the arrows of the Odd-arrowed One, they forgot their long sorrow. And though wounded by nails and teeth, they sighed deeply as if in fear. May this fine song of Ramananda Raya increase the joy of Rudra, lord of elephants.8

Shashimukhi. Lady, this seems to me almost incongruous.

Madanika. How so?

Shashimukhi. Where did they get such skill in love?

Madanika. Ah, simple girl!

Verse 29

उपदिशति गुरुर्गुरुप्रयत्ना-
त्तदपि च कालवशात्प्रयाति पाकम् ।
इति किल नियताः समस्तविद्याः
सुरतकलाः स्वत एव सम्भवन्ति ॥ २९ ॥

upadiśati gururguruprayatnā-
ttadapi ca kālavaśātprayāti pākam |
iti kila niyatāḥ samastavidyāḥ
suratakalāḥ svata eva sambhavanti || 29 ||

upadiśati — instructs; guruḥ — the teacher; guru-prayatnāt — with great effort; tad api ca — and that too; kāla-vaśāt — in course of time; prayāti pākam — ripens; iti — thus; kila — indeed; niyatāḥ — is ordered; samasta-vidyāḥ — all sciences; surata-kalāḥ — the arts of love; svataḥ eva — of themselves; sambhavanti — arise.

29A teacher instructs with great effort, and the teaching ripens in time — so it is with all the sciences; but the arts of love arise of themselves.9

Verse 30

अत्रान्तरे सुरतकेलिकलासु तासु
प्रायेण शिक्षित इवैष शशी चिरेण ।
योग्यां ततः किमपि कर्तुमिव प्रकामं
संसेवते स्म चरमां दिशमादरेण ॥ ३० ॥

atrāntare suratakelikalāsu tāsu
prāyeṇa śikṣita ivaiṣa śaśī cireṇa |
yogyāṁ tataḥ kimapi kartumiva prakāmaṁ
saṁsevate sma caramāṁ diśamādareṇa || 30 ||

30Meanwhile the moon, having long, it seems, been schooled in those arts of love-play, now, as if to put its training into practice, devotedly clung to the western quarter.10

pañca-iṣoḥ — of the Five-arrowed; viśikha-āvalībhiḥ — by rows of arrows; abhitaḥ — on every side; nistakṣyamāṇe — being lacerated; tanau — when the body; ānanda-eka-nidānam — the sole source of bliss; eṇa-nayanā — the doe-eyed; prāptā — obtained; prasādāt tava — by your grace; bhūyaḥ — again; sā iyam — this; alambhi — was obtained; kācana — a certain; dṛśoḥ — for the eyes; pīyūṣa-dhārā — stream of nectar; mayā — by Me; kiṁ vā — what; ataḥ param — beyond this; asti — is there; devi — O lady; bhuvane — in the world; kiṁcit — anything; priyam — dear; mādṛśām — to such as Me.

61When the arrows of the Five-arrowed One were piercing Me on every side, the doe-eyed one, sole source of My bliss, was won for Me by your grace; and again I have gained a stream of nectar for My eyes. What, lady, can there be in the world more pleasing still for such as Me?

Song 21 — in raga Mangala-gurjari.

पिकविधुमधुमधुपावलिचरितं

pariṇata-śārada-śaśadhara-vadanā — with a face like the full autumn moon; militā — has united; pāṇi-tale — hand in hand; guru-madanā — filled with great love; devi — O lady; kim — what; iha — here; param — further; asti — is; mad-iṣṭam — desired by Me; bahu-tara-sukṛta-phalitam — the fruit of many good deeds; anudiṣṭam — has come unbidden; pika-vidhu-madhu-madhupa-āvali-caritam — the doings of cuckoos, moon, spring and swarms of bees; racayati — make; mām — Me; adhunā — now; sukha-bharitam — filled with happiness; praṇayatu — may it bring; rudra-nṛpe — to King Rudra; sukham — happiness; amṛtam — immortality; rāmānanda-bhaṇita-hari-ramitam — the play of Hari spoken by Ramananda.

62The moon-faced one, like the full autumn moon, filled with great love, has joined Me, and her hand is in Mine. Lady, what else here could be desired by Me? The fruit of many good deeds has come of itself. (Refrain.) The cuckoos, the moon, spring and the swarms of bees — all now fill Me with happiness. May this, spoken by Ramananda — the play of Hari — bring King Rudra happiness and immortality.18

And still, let this be so:

śraddhā-baddha-matiḥ — his mind bound by faith; mama — My; pratidinam — every day; gopāla-līlasya — of Gopala at play; yaḥ — who; saṁseveta — serves; rahasyam — secret; etat — this; atulam — incomparable; līlā-amṛtam — nectar of pastimes; lola-dhīḥ — eager; tasmin — on him; mad-gata-mānase — whose mind is given to Me; kila — indeed; kṛpā-dṛṣṭyā — with a gracious glance; bhavatyā — by you; sadā — always; bhāvyam — it should be; yena — so that; nija-īpsitām — desired; vraja-vane — in the forests of Vraja; siddhim — perfection; samāpnoti — attains; saḥ — he.

63Whoever, his mind bound by faith, eagerly serves day by day this incomparable secret, the nectar of the play of Me, Gopala — on him, whose mind is given to Me, may you always look with a gracious eye, so that he may attain the perfection he desires in the forests of Vraja.19

Madanika. So be it.

(Exeunt omnes.)

End of the Fifth Act, "Radha-sangama".

Thus ends the drama "Sri Jagannatha-vallabha", composed by Ramananda Raya.

Notes

  1. Mandākrāntā metre. Shashimukhi sees Madanika (the Forest-goddess), who has not slept all night. "Her feet falter" — the print reads maṁdayāsa, corrected in the edition's errata to mandanyāsa ("slow step").
  2. Madanika, sleepless all night, resembles a woman after love-play. This is a hint, explained later: she spent the whole night watching the play of Radha and Krishna (verse 14). The first line of the song is unclear in places. For Gaudiya Vaishnavas the joy of the sakhis lies in arranging and beholding the meeting of Radha and Krishna, not in enjoying Krishna themselves (cf. CC Madhya 8.206–208).
  3. Śikhariṇī metre. A description of dawn (prabhāta), obligatory in Sanskrit drama. The end of the third line is unclear in the print.
  4. The last line is unclear. The edition's Hindi translation reads: "what clever woman does not imitate this cakravaka?" In the morning the female cakravaka is reunited with her mate after the night's separation.
  5. An allegory: the female bee who took a reflection for her beloved and then sees the real one is an image of the mingling of conflicting emotions (bhāva-śābalya).
  6. Śārdūla-vikrīḍita metre. Stupor (stambha) and trembling (kampa) are sāttvika-bhāvas, bodily signs of ecstatic love: Radha at first took Krishna's stupor for indifference and only by His trembling understood His love. The beginning of the third line is unclear in the print.
  7. Here and further on (verses 24–36) Ramananda describes the highest stage of madhura-rasa, sambhoga, the union of Radha and Krishna, in the language of classical poetics. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati stresses that these pastimes (aprākṛta-līlā) have nothing in common with worldly relationships. Their participants are Bhagavan Himself and His own pleasure-potency (hlādinī-śakti). Such descriptions are meant only for devotees whose hearts are purified, and they must not be understood in a worldly way or imitated (cf. CC Adi 4.164–171: kama and prema differ as iron and gold). Ramananda himself calls them a "secret" in his closing verse 63, meant for those who serve Gopala's pastimes with faith.
  8. The print has niśvasitāyatabhītaṁ, whose sense is unclear. The edition's Hindi translation reads "began to breathe heavily in fear": the agitation came not from pain but from the fullness of love. Cf. note 7.
  9. Puṣpitāgrā metre. Shashimukhi is surprised, since Radha and Krishna are still young. Madanika replies that love needs no teaching. For Gaudiya Vaishnavas this reflects the eternal, self-manifest nature of their love: it is not acquired but abides eternally in Radha and Krishna.
  10. Vasanta-tilakā metre. The moon "clung to the western quarter", that is, it set and dawn came — a play on the image of the moon as a lover.
  11. Śārdūla-vikrīḍita metre. Returning in the morning, Radha fears being seen. Lines 3–4 are partly unclear in the print and are rendered by the sense and the edition's Hindi translation.
  12. Śārdūla-vikrīḍita metre. Radha fears the harmless (a stump, a crow, light) more than real danger; likewise, meeting her beloved, she is more anxious than in separation, from fear of being seen and from the fullness of feeling.
  13. The song continues the description of sambhoga (see note 7). The sense of "by the gentle movement of her lotus feet" (printed mṛdupadakamalalavehā) is unclear. The edition's Hindi translation reads: "it is at once understood from the gentle movement of her lotus feet". The closing line in the original is an appeal to the audience: "make your hearts free of fault". The connoisseurs are to hear this with a pure heart.
  14. The slaying of Arishtasura is told in Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.36. "Prop of the earth" alludes to the lifting of Govardhana Hill. "Sacrificial post of the appeasement of Shakra" means Krishna's arm as the support that averts Indra's wrath. Ramananda joins this pastime to the dawn after the night in the grove. In the Bhāgavata Arishta comes in the evening, but as a dramatist Ramananda is free in ordering the events.
  15. Śārdūla-vikrīḍita metre. Madanika despairs, thinking Krishna in danger. "Mother Devaki": according to the edition's gloss, this is Yashoda's second name ("Nanda's wife has two names, Yashoda and Devaki"), as she is also called in some Puranas. "Shri, take up the vow" means "take the vow of widowhood".
  16. Śārdūla-vikrīḍita metre. Krishna hurled Arishta "like a ball": in the Bhāgavata (10.36) Krishna, seizing the bull by the horns, threw it down and killed it.
  17. "Chosen by Victory herself" — literally "embraced by the goddess of Victory at her svayaṁvara", the ceremony at which a bride chooses her husband.
  18. The last song of the drama, sung by Krishna. The twenty-one songs of the drama are passages 1.4, 1.22, 1.28, 1.37, 2.20, 2.24, 2.35, 2.46, 3.3, 3.8, 3.15, 3.34, 4.2, 4.15, 4.25, 4.37, 4.51, 5.3, 5.25, 5.36 and 5.62 of the edition. They are written in the style of Jayadeva's Gīta-govinda, each with a raga, a refrain (dhruva) and a closing line naming the author and dedicated to Prataparudra.
  19. Śārdūla-vikrīḍita metre. The closing benediction (bharata-vākya). Krishna asks the Forest-goddess (Madanika) to look graciously on those who with faith "serve" this "secret, the nectar of Gopala's play" (hearing, singing or staging it), so that they may attain perfection in Vraja. For Gaudiya Vaishnavas this points to the path of rāgānugā-bhakti under the guidance of Radha's companions. According to the CC, Mahaprabhu sang and heard the "songs of Raya's drama" day and night with Svarupa Damodara and Ramananda Raya (Madhya 2.77) and relished its verses in His ecstatic moods (Antya 20.67).
